cohort: The study retrospectively evaluated 58,897 patients who gave birth in a hospital between January 2013 and December 2022, focusing on primary C/S rates after excluding 14,045 patients with a history of C/S.
finding: Male fetuses were associated with a significantly higher rate of primary cesarean section compared to female fetuses in both adolescent and adult maternal age groups.
mod_finding: A significantly higher primary cesarean section rate was observed in male fetuses compared to female fetuses in both adolescent and adult maternal age groups.
